body:
**Raamdeo Agrawal / Motilal Oswal: QGLP and the Wealth Creation Studies**
- **QGLP (said by the firm).** Quality of business and management, Growth in earnings, Longevity of quality and growth, and a favourable Price. "Buy Right" means "buying quality companies at a reasonable price," and "Sit Tight" means staying invested to realise full growth potential. The firm frames the price leg as buying a good business at a fair price, not a fair business at a good price. — [Motilal Oswal PMS investment philosophy](https://pms.motilaloswalmf.com/about-us/investment-philosophy)
- **100x study (2014).** [primary, not re-fetched]
  - Results in the study: about 47 stocks did 100x over the study span, out of a universe of about 3,500. On average they took about 12 years, which is roughly a 47% CAGR. Most 100x stocks gave multi-year windows to buy in. — [Outlook Business interview](https://www.outlookbusiness.com/interview/how-to-spot-a-100-bagger-744); [Hedge Fund Alpha, "100x power of growth"](https://hedgefundalpha.com/strategies/100x-power-growth-wealth-creation/)
  - Framework: the study added **S (Size)** to make **SQGLP**, favouring a small market cap at the start. Agrawal's "100x" formula is the twin engine again: earnings growth combined with P/E rerating.
- **Agrawal's own framing (said).** He says "100X is a rare phenomenon." — [Outlook Business](https://www.outlookbusiness.com/markets/interview/value-investors-do-not-talk-or-focus-too-much-on-growth-2482)
- **QGLP screen pass rate.** One QGLP screen kept only 24 of 531 investible companies (<5%). — [5paisa summary of Agrawal's philosophy](https://www.5paisa.com/blog/raamdeo-agrawal-investment-philosophy-and-latest-portfolio-2026)
- **Long-run lessons (said by the firm).** Across the studies, Motilal repeatedly states three lessons:
  - Wealth is created when you buy at low P/E and the stock then rerates: "the biggest wealth is created when growth and rerating combine."
  - "Value migration" across sectors.
  - High returns on equity combined with earnings growth.
  - Source: [Wealth Creation Study 2009–14](https://www.motilaloswal.com/site/rreports/HTML/635542588369519988/index.htm) [primary, opened only as a search result]
- **30th study (Dec 2025, covering 2020–25).**
  - The top 100 wealth creators added a record ₹148 trillion.
  - Wealth creation grew at a 38% CAGR, against 21% for the Sensex.
  - The top 10 fastest creators returned about 88% CAGR, against 24% for the Nifty TRI: ₹1 crore became ₹24 crore.
  - Financials were the largest sector, followed by industrials, capital markets, technology and utilities.
  - The theme is "India – The Multi-Trillion Dollar Opportunity." The study expects large caps to outperform in the medium term.
  - Sources: [Motilal Oswal press release](https://www.motilaloswalgroup.com/Media-Room/Press-Release/-/india’s-biggest-wealth-boom-rs148-trillion-ad/FS/20796); [Thematic study Dec 2025](https://www.motilaloswal.com/site/rreports/html/639014785692549159/index.htm); [Outlook Money](https://www.outlookmoney.com/amp/story/invest/biggest-and-fastest-wealth-creators-since-2020-top-stocks-that-turned-rs-1-crore-into-rs-24-crore)
  - These are Motilal's own calculations and were not independently verified.

body: The price range is roughly right: about ₹50–190 adjusted in 2008–2016, and about ₹4,100–4,750 in 2026, which is 25–90x depending on the start point. The cause and the timing in the user's version are wrong. The stock was **dead money for about 8 years (2008–2016)**. The multibagger move began only in **2016–17** and was driven by **premiumisation, deleveraging and operating leverage**. No 2008 "UBL issue" caused it. "UBL" is United Breweries Ltd, the Kingfisher beer company, which is not Radico's spirits competitor. The user probably means the UB Group / United Spirits (USL) / Vijay Mallya saga, which ran 2012–2016 (Kingfisher Airlines collapse, then Diageo taking control of USL in 2013). I found no source showing investors bought Radico in 2008 on a UB thesis.

`theme:sector-power-utilities-renewables` · confidence: single-source · tickers: NTPC, POWERGRID, TATAPOWER, ADANIGREEN, JSWENERGY, NHPC, IEX, NTPCGREEN

**How it makes money:** Regulated RoE on asset base (utilities, transmission); contracted PPA returns (renewables); spot-price exposure (merchant/IEX).

**Metrics that matter:**
- Regulated equity / capitalisation
- Commissioned vs pipeline MW
- PLF (thermal) / CUF (RE)
- PPA tariff vs capex (equity IRR)
- Net debt/EBITDA
- Discom receivable days
- Merchant share & realisation

**Value chain and where margins sit:** Fuel (coal/gas) or equipment (modules, turbines, BESS) -> generation -> transmission (ISTS/STU) -> discoms (financially weakest link) -> consumers. Regulated transmission is the steadiest; generation with merchant upside is the most volatile; discoms destroy value.

**Cycle drivers:** Demand growth, weather, coal supply, rates, equipment prices, policy (ALMM, BCD, ISTS waiver phase-out), discom payment discipline.

**Lead indicators (public India data):**
- CEA monthly generation & installed capacity reports
- Grid-India daily PSP report (peak demand)
- IEX daily DAM/RTM prices & volumes
- MNRE monthly RE capacity
- CEA daily coal stock report
- PFC annual discom integrated ratings

**What separated winners from losers:** Winners: contracted or regulated returns, low-cost financing, execution track record, timely merchant positioning. Losers: untied capacity with imported fuel (2010–13), aggressive tariff bids, related-party EPC/fund diversion (Gensol 2025), high receivables.

**Valuation ranges and peaks/troughs:** Regulated: 1.0–1.3x P/B at troughs (2019–20), ~2–2.5x at peaks (2024). RE IPPs 15–25x EV/EBITDA; peak RE multiples in 2021–22 and 2024. IEX P/E 30–60x.

**Current state (Nov 2026):** Record peak 270.8 GW (21 May 2026); Q2 FY27 peak ~270 GW (16 Jul 2026, +18% YoY). Q2 FY27: coal PLF 68% (62% a year ago), ~7 GW RE vs 0.8 GW thermal added; ICRA FY27 gross additions ~50 GW vs 61.6 GW FY26. Early Oct 2026 demand +23% YoY, IEX ~₹7.7/unit; 85 plants with critical coal stocks (1 Oct).

**Classic traps:**
- Pipeline GW announcements vs commissioned MW
- Transmission/curtailment risk on RE
- Low module prices cutting tariffs (and returns) for everyone
- Promoter-pledged RE platforms

body:
- **id:** `thesis:paper-call:KAYNES:q3fy27-revenue-1050cr-plus`
- **Method:** flags-judgment context · **P(ours)** 0.38 · **P(base)** 0.45 · resolve by 2027-02-28
- **Evidence:** Q2 FY27 call (16-Nov-2026): consolidated revenue ₹952.5 cr, EBITDA ₹125.6 cr (13.2%), PAT ₹39.8 cr; H1 revenue ₹1,898.7 cr, EBITDA margin 14.1%. Flags: change of auditor (new auditor Walker Chandiok & Co); FY26 and Q1 FY27 comparatives restated (FY26 revenue ₹3,620 cr→₹3,680 cr, FY26 EBITDA margin 15.8%→14.2%; bill-discounted receivables moved into borrowings); limited-review conclusion 'not modified' but carries an emphasis of matter on the restatement. Smart-meter business deliberately throttled: revenue there 'purely based on the amount of collection', target total smart-meter receivables <₹750 cr (₹1,091 cr at Sep-26 vs ₹1,402 cr Jun-26); H1 smart-meter revenue ~₹270 cr vs ~₹960 cr in all of FY26. Management: 'confident of growing the electronic business… more than 30% for FY27', 'second half is stronger… in revenue and margins', OSAT revenue started and PCB unit contributes from Q3. Screener (₹ cr): sales Dec-24 661, Mar-25 984, Jun-25 673, Sep-25 912, Dec-25 804, Mar-26 1,243, Jun-26 946, Sep-26 953 (+4% YoY); OPM 13% in Q2.
- **Why our number differs from base:** The flags here (auditor change, restatement, receivable reclassification) have teeth for revenue specifically because management is now explicitly trading revenue for collections in the meter business. ₹1,050 cr needs +10% QoQ while the highest-margin, previously fastest-growing line shrinks; new OSAT/PCB units are just ramping. We set our number below a naive 'H2 is seasonally bigger and management says stronger' reading.
- **Base-rate reasoning:** Kaynes' Q3 revenue was below Q2 in FY26 (804 vs 912) but above it in FY25 (661 vs 572); a naive forecaster taking management's 'stronger H2' at face value puts ≥10% QoQ growth near 45%.
- **Resolution rule:** YES if Kaynes Technology's consolidated revenue from operations for the quarter ended 31-Dec-2026 (results filing; equivalently screener.in consolidated 'Sales') is ≥₹1,050 cr. Use the figure as first reported, not later restatements.
- **Resolution source:** Kaynes Technology Q3 FY27 results (NSE filing) / screener.in consolidated quarterly table
- **Sources used:** https://nsearchives.nseindia.in/corporate/KAYNESTECH_20112026152655_TranscriptoftheEarningAnnouncement.pdf; https://www.screener.in/company/KAYNES/consolidated/
- **Confidence of evidence:** verified
